parts.passage:
The telescope is an instrument that allows us to see distant objects closer. We can view objects that are far beyond the range of our eyes. This instrument has opened a new door for us to study space from the Earth and changed our understanding of the universe. With the help of a telescope, it was proved that the Earth revolves around the Sun, and the old geocentric concept was dropped.

The telescope is one of the instruments that was not invented by a scientist. Instead, it was invented by a Dutch eyeglass maker Hans Lippershey. While working with lenses, he brought two lenses in front of each other and found that distant objects were seen closer through them. Then he fitted two lenses (a convex and a concave) in a tube and made the first working telescope. His telescope magnified the distant objects about three times. He applied for the patent, but officials said to him that this instrument was too simple to copy, and they didn't issue the patent.

A great scientist Galileo Galilei heard about this new invention. He started to build his own telescope, without ever seeing the Dutchman's instrument. He made an improved version of the telescope which magnified the distant object eight times. With further improvements, he made another telescope with a power of 20. He turned his telescope to the sky and watched the planets, and their moons. He proved that the Earth and other planets in the solar system revolve around the Sun. Galileo continued to improve his telescopes and made one with the power of 100, which helped him to study the sky further. There was a limit in further increasing the magnification because it decreased the field of view, combined with spherical and chromatic aberrations. This prompted a need for an entirely new telescope design that could eliminate these problems.

parts.passage:
Music is a special way people talk to each other, often when they dance or tell stories. Even though it can make us feel strong emotions, it doesn't need words to make sense. Music can be considered as a form of communication through sound. It is so much more than just a source of entertainment; it is an important part of our lifetime learning. However, just listening to music may have a smaller effect than actually playing music. This is much the same as the way that playing sports will improve your physical condition more than simply watching sports.

Just like your muscles, your brain gets stronger the more you exercise it. There are some important things that happen in the brain when we play music. Firstly, the auditory system processes sound more effectively after musical training. People can detect smaller differences in frequency (the number of sound waves per second), making both speech and music easier to hear. Brain areas that control instrument-related muscles and body parts (such as the fingers, the mouth, etc.) grow in size. More neurons in the brain are devoted to fine-tuning muscle movement in these areas. Studies also show that better musical ability is related to higher reading scores, suggesting a link between how well we hear speech and how well we can map speech sounds to letters. Moreover, playing music together can foster social connections among the participants. It can also enhance socio-emotional awareness, which is the ability to identify, manage, and express emotions constructively. A good example of this is that very young children are more likely to interact positively with people they play music with.

The function of music extends beyond fostering personal development. It can be a way that we express our identities: the music we play, or even listen to, can be a way of telling the world, our peers, our parents, and our friends something about who we are. For example, imagine someone who loves listening to fast and energetic beats. They might be someone who enjoys excitement and being active. On the other hand, someone who prefers calm and soothing melodies might appreciate peace and tranquility. The music we connect with often reflects our emotions, interests, and the things that make us happy.
